anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moved all three facts from fails to holds, and nothing Before kept was lost. For same-flaw and independent, Before kept the note file, its hash and reject on record after the overrule, whereas After marks P1/P2/P3 as `(dispositioned: overruled)` without resolving them, deletes the note, sets reject to null once no open approach blocker remains, and in B leaves L1 as the sole entry in `blocker_numbers` with an initial deliver/assess/stop menu and no merge. For mapping, both outputs resolve against the current `[{n:1,ids:[P4]}]` and re-show the same menu with no state change or question marker, but Before's bare-`overrule` refusal said "Overrule needs the number of the problem to set aside, and the current report lists only problem 1", which steers the reader towards `overrule 1` on the ineligible P4. After's refusals ("Problem 2 is not in the current report, so nothing was set aside" and "No problem number was given, so nothing was set aside") avoid that. To keep this stable, the wording should say explicitly that a refusal sentence states only why the command was not applied and never names a valid problem number or implies an overrule would work, and that the remark about P4 being unattempted belongs only in the inspection table, as After has it. It should also keep explicit the rule that note deletion and reject clearing happen exactly when the last open approach contributor is overruled, and that the one-sentence set-aside line and the fresh-judgement note for a later run are stated; After put the later-run sentence outside the rendered report, which is fine here but worth pinning down.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before failed all three facts because it treated `overrule` as undefined and rendered no dispositions, reports or menus. After moves all three, and nothing Before held was lost. For same-flaw, A marks P1/P2/P3 overruled rather than resolved, deletes the note, nulls reject, names the set-aside conflict in one sentence, renders final with merge recommended, and says a later run judges afresh. For independent, B lifts only P1/P2/P3, keeps unattempted L1 as the sole blocker, and renders initial with deliver/assess/stop, no merge and no resumed course. For mapping, both C commands get a one-sentence refusal against the current [P4] mapping and the same menu, with no state change, no question marker and no overrule suggestion for P4. Two things in After are fragile. First, it narrates `rm` and three `gh` refresh commands as if executed, although the entry says to use no tools and the refresh already matches; a stricter reader could count that against the 'no write or dispatch' clause. Wording that says the note deletion and null reject are recorded state changes, and that the already-matching pre-menu refresh is reused, would be safer. Second, the C refusal turns repeat the gate line and the 'I recommend deliver' sentence. That is acceptable as part of the same menu, but the wording should make explicit that a refusal is one sentence plus the menu, not a re-rendered report, so the summary and problem paragraphs are never copied in.
